name: Muza (Muzahid Abdullah)
origin_city: New York City (diaspora; born Balaganj, Osmani Nagar, Sylhet)

global_influences.evidence: Muza has cited Habib Wahid's songs as his direct musical inspiration, indicating a primarily domestic (rather than purely Western) lineage of folk-electronic fusion influence carried into the Bangladeshi-American diaspora.

Muza layers traditional deshi instruments alongside non-traditional instruments (ukulele, flute) with electronic beats and urban production techniques, directly paralleling Habib Wahid's folk-EDM fusion approach but from a US diaspora production context.

local_adaptation_notes: Raised in New York City from early childhood after emigrating from Sylhet, Muza's music specifically foregrounds Sylheti folk vocal styles and traditional deshi instrumentation fused with electronic/urban pop production — a diaspora-specific variant of the folk-fusion pattern also seen in Habib Wahid's domestic work, achieving viral reach with songs like 'Noya Daman,' 'Beni Khuley,' and 'Jhumka' that have collectively drawn hundreds of millions of views/streams.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period: began songwriting at age eight, drawing on Bengali cinema and cultural traditions and multilingual exposure (including Arabic). Career development: partnered with producer G' Anomaly to build a signature deshi-instrument-plus-electronic-beat sound. Breakthrough period: viral commercial success with 'Noya Daman,' 'Beni Khuley,' and 'Jhumka,' establishing Muza as a leading diaspora voice within Bangladeshi pop/folk-fusion.
concert_culture_notes: As a diaspora-based artist (New York City), Muza's primary visibility and reach have been driven by streaming/viral video distribution rather than a domestic Bangladeshi touring circuit — a pattern shared with Stoic Bliss in the Hip-Hop genre.
listener_community_notes: Bridges Bangladeshi diaspora and domestic pop/folk-fusion listener communities; his Sylheti-specific folk material also connects to regional folk listener networks distinct from the pan-Bangla mainstream pop audience.
